source.title: From Latent Space to Jacobian Space: Measuring, Evading, and Training Against Safety-Content Accessibility

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures transport of a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction and steers along it. It concludes that amplification is descriptive rather than causally load-bearing for J-space danger recognition, and reports that training can change refusal behavior and J-space recognition in different directions. It does not perform the original refusal-direction ablation or addition.
record.gate_note: The paper does not ablate the difference-in-means direction from every layer and position, add it to induce refusals, or measure general capability after such an intervention. Its steering outcome is J-space SafetyAUC, not refusal behavior. GCG attacks suppress the J-space monitor rather than the specified latent refusal direction, so their attack and monitor results are not rows for V3. Abliteration is mentioned and an abliterated checkpoint is measured, but the paper does not report its refusal behavior. Per-layer profiles and some correlations are shown in figures without complete numeric values; only the paper's separately stated numeric results are recorded.
record.test_reason: The study uses an Arditi-style difference-in-means direction only as a tool for its transport-amplification metric and for steering. Every outcome is J-space SafetyAUC or amplification, not refusal behavior after ablating or adding the direction. The DPO study reports refusal rates but never extracts, ablates or tests a refusal direction. So no version is tested. V7 asks whether training decides that one removable direction exists, and nothing here measures existence or removability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that training provenance reshapes J-space accessibility but 'tuned ⇒ more accessible' does not hold below 1.5B. At 0.5B, DPO installs refusal while J-space recognition falls to chance. Amplification of the mean safety direction is descriptive, not causal, for recognition. Prompt-side J-space monitors are evaded by GCG suffixes, and only a learned monitor resists adaptive attack. They do not test whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures Jacobian-space danger recognition and transport of a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction, and uses activation steering and DPO training. It does not use the original all-layer/all-position refusal-direction ablation or refusal-inducing addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Lens-fit seed has a first-order effect; corpus choice and target window shift absolute SafetyAUC; tuned-versus-base ordering is unstable for several smaller pairs. Training effects vary by model scale. Steering result reported at layer 16 of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: At 0.5B, LoRA-DPO raises refusal from 0.05 to 0.96 while J-space SafetyAUC falls from 0.728 to 0.541. At 135M and 1.5B both rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioral refusal and output-accessible danger recognition can move independently under preference tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the diff-in-means safety direction at layer 16 of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct shifts SafetyAUC only slightly (0.807 at α=−4, 0.761 at +4, vs 0.787). The layer-profile correlation with amplification is −0.47 (base −0.07).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transport of the mean harmful-minus-benign direction does not account for J-space danger recognition.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes decode danger at about 0.996 in both base (non-refusing) and instruct models (Table 12). An abliterated Qwen3-1.7B shows below-chance J-space SafetyAUC (0.293 bf16 vs 0.798 base; Table 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent harmfulness information persists regardless of refusal training, while output-accessible recognition depends on it and collapses under abliteration.

fits_no_version.finding: GCG suffixes suppress a prompt-side J-space monitor at no behavioral cost; only a learned monitor resists its adaptive re-attack.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: J-space safety monitors are evadable by discrete suffix search.

record.problems: The study uses its own English lexicons rather than JADR's original lists; absolute SafetyAUC is instrument-sensitive, with shifts up to 0.37 under random half-lexicon resampling. The safe control is XSTest only because OKTest prompts were unavailable. Training has one seed for the Qwen models, and the reported 0.5B divergence is described as instrument-dependent. Chat-template differences between base and tuned checkpoints are not separately ablated. The steering evidence concerns J-space recognition rather than refusal behavior, and does not test the original ablation/addition claim.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying claim-version results were omitted for the 60-row limit. Attack, monitor-ladder, transfer, quantization, and general probe results are excluded because they test J-space monitoring or related constructs rather than the specified latent refusal direction and its refusal behavior. Figure-only layer profiles are not transcribed as numeric rows.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction with refusal-rate or capability outcomes.
The abliterated Qwen3-1.7B checkpoint is measured only for J-space SafetyAUC; its refusal behavior is not reported.
GCG suffixes target a J-space monitor, not the refusal direction.
No test of whether training creates a single removable refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 labels and links should be dropped. Refusal rates are a 100-prompt held-out measure without a refusal-direction analysis. Absolute SafetyAUC shifts by up to 0.37 under lexicon resampling. Qwen DPO runs use one seed.

versions.untested_parts: No all-layer/all-position ablation or addition of the direction, no refusal-rate outcome from steering that direction, and no general-capability check after removal.
No weight-edit abliteration is performed or evaluated for refusal behavior.
The attacks suppress a J-space monitor readout, not the specified latent refusal direction; no training against that direction's ablation is tested.
The study says danger recognition is not reducible to transport of the mean safety direction, but does not test affine, cone, or multiple refusal directions against refusal behavior.
The study contrasts J-space danger separability and refusal behavior, but does not measure a model's harmfulness judgment as distinct from its refusal decision.
No transfer of the specified direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.

The study measures training-related changes in refusal rates, J-space SafetyAUC, and transport of a difference-in-means direction. It does not test whether training determines the existence or removability of a single refusal direction.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The reported LoRA-DPO tuning runs across SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B
reader_labels.reason: Training changes refusal rates, but its effect on J-space recognition varies: at 0.5B refusal rises while SafetyAUC falls to near chance; at other scales the recognition result differs. These results do not establish whether a removable single refusal direction exists (rows r17–r32).
